pageCache.text:
ACERs (After School Provision) and Breakfast Club
Our breakfast club runs daily at Southwood School, offering a choice of breakfast options (cereals, toast, juice, milk). We provide a range of activities for the children to keep them occupied until the start of the school day.
Children are able to come into school from 8am at the earliest through the main front door and should be in school no later than 8.20am, so they have enough time to have their breakfast.
Breakfast Club costs £1.50 per day, paid on the day, or in advance if you prefer. Children from Downs Barn and Germander Park are taken to their respective schools before the start of the school day on the school minibus.
For those with children at Downs Barn or Germander Park, please can we ask that you book in advance through the school office and advise the day/days that your child will be attending breakfast club. This is particularly important as we need to staff accordingly for the transportation. For children at Southwood there is no need to pre-book, children can turn up as and when you require.
Please complete a registration form for your child so we ensure we have up to date contact, medical and dietary information.
ACERS (After School Provision)
Acers provides after school care for children from nursery age through to year 6 on the premises of Southwood School. All our staff are trained to the required level and hold Paediatric or Basic First Aid qualifications. Children are transported from Downs Barn/Germander Park Schools to Southwood School using the school minibus. On occasions where the minibus is not available children will be walking using the Walking Bus.
A variety of activities are available during sessions, catering for the variety of ages, e.g., art and craft, books and magazines, ipads, board games, outdoor games and activities, films etc. A quiet area is also available for children to do their homework. A healthy snack and drink is provided between 4.00-4.30pm, such as toast, fruit, juice, milk etc. Your registration form gives us information about any food allergies. Snacks served comply with the Government’s School Food Standards, and our staff have received food hygiene training.
Payment will be invoiced weekly, to be paid within 7 days.
Snack session to 4.30pm
Collection between 4.30-5.00pm
Collection between 5.00-5.30pm
Collection between 5.30-6pm
Please note there is a late collection charge of £10.00 after 6pm.
If you think you might be interested in using Acers at any time, please complete the registration form, read and sign the Code of Conduct and return both documents to school as soon as possible. Please note, children will not be able to attend Acers without these first being returned to school.
All sessions must be booked using the weekly ParentMail Booking form or at least 24 hours in advance by calling the school office. This is to ensure adequate staffing and the safety of all children in our care. We require at least 24 hours’ notice of cancellation. Any cancellations within 24 hours will be charged at £5 per child.

Attendance
As you will be aware, at Southwood school, we are highly committed to making sure children’s attendance is as high as possible. Whilst there are some occasions where children need to be taken out of school for a genuinely exceptional circumstance (which will be recognised by the school) in general, children must not be taken out of school during term time. This includes holidays.
If a child is has an unauthorised absence for 5 days in a row (which is recorded as 10 school sessions – morning and afternoon), a fixed penalty fine may be issued. Repeated unauthorised absences over a period of time may also lead to a fixed penalty fine. If a child misses 10 individual school sessions within a three month period, a fine may be issued.
If your child will not be at school because they are ill, or for another valid reason, please telephone the school before 9am. If we haven't received a phone call, we will telephone you to check where your child is (additional contact numbers may be used if we cannot contact you on the first priority number).
The following guidance regarding attendance is from Milton Keynes Council: The importance of regular school attendance Regular attendance at school is vital to help children achieve and get the best possible start in life. Children who frequently miss school often fall behind. In fact, there is a strong link between regular school attendance and achieving good grades at GCSE - having an attendance rate of 80% is equivalent to missing a day a week
Your responsibilities as a parent Children must receive a full time education between the school term after their fifth birthday and the last Friday in June in the school year they turn 16 (Y11). If your child fails to attend school regularly you may be guilty of a criminal offence and this could result in a prosecution. All Milton Keynes schools have their own attendance policies and are responsible for managing pupil attendance. Authorised and unauthorised absence If your child cannot attend school, you should contact the school as early as possible to explain why your child needs to be absent and to obtain permission to ensure the absence is authorised. Only the school can authorise your child’s absence. An authorised absence is where the school has given approval in advance or has accepted an explanation for the absence afterwards. In most cases this will be due to your child being ill. If your child has a lot of absence due to illness the school may ask for GP or other medical evidence to enable them to make a decision about authorising the absence. If the school does not accept the reason for absence or no reason is given the absence will be marked as “unauthorised” and you will place yourself at risk of prosecution or of receiving another financial sanction.
Medical appointments Try to arrange appointments during school holidays, at weekends or after school hours. Naturally, there will be times when this is not possible but you must try to give as much advance warning as possible and take the appointment letter or card into school to ensure they are aware of the absence and the reasons for it.
Religious festivals Ask your school in advance for time off for religious reasons. Only the day of the actual religious festival/celebration will be “authorised”. Persistent Lateness after the Register has close If your child is persistently late after the register the school can ask the Local Authority to issue a Fixed Penalty Notice. An explanation of Fixed Penalty Notices is given below.
Holidays/Leave during term time Schools are no longer allowed to authorise requests for children to be taken out of school in term time unless there are “exceptional circumstances”. If you take a holiday which is not authorised by the school then they may refer the matter to the Local Authority who will consider the issue of a Fixed Penalty Notice.Fixed Penalty Notices (FPN) are issued to each parent and are for each child. A FPN is £60 if paid within 21 days, and £120 if paid between 22 and 28 days. If the fine is not paid, parents will be prosecuted in the magistrates’ court. If a FPN is issued, it will be one fine to cover the whole period of the absence. So the fine would be the same amount for an absence of five days or 10 days. Please refer to our FAQ’s for further information. (DOC, 68KB). You can make a payment for a Fixed Penalty Notice by selecting Fixed Penalty Notices – School Attendance Payment on our 'Pay for it' page found here. You will need the serial number of the FPN to make an on-line payment - this will start with the letters SA.
Please understand that fixed penalty fines will only be issued when parents/carers have not adhered to the school’s Attendance Policy.
